title: Gregory of Nyssa, Dogmatic Treatises etc. (NPNF II-5)
author: Gregory of Nyssa
description: Gregory of Nyssa: Dogmatic Treatises, etc., Volume V of the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, Second Series, edited by Philip Schaff and Henry Wace (1893), translated by William Moore and Henry Austin Wilson. Gregory of Nyssa (c. 335-395), one of the Cappadocian Fathers with his brother Basil and Gregory Nazianzen, was among the most philosophically gifted early theologians. The volume includes his long treatise Against Eunomius defending the full divinity of the Son, works on the Trinity and Holy Spirit ('Not three Gods'), the Great Catechism, On the Making of Man, On the Soul and the Resurrection (a dialogue with his sister Macrina), On Infants' Early Deaths, On Virginity and selected letters. Gregory's teaching on God's infinity, the soul's endless ascent (epektasis), and universal restoration shaped Christian mysticism from Dionysius to the Orthodox tradition.
